fatal_errors: The proposed shear-induced transient ductile phase is not observed or supported for WTaTiVZr; the target interpretation instead invokes solid-solution/lattice-distortion strengthening and Ti-V-Zr-assisted plasticity and crack resistance.

The initial microstructure is incorrectly assumed to be homogeneous and predominantly single-phase, whereas the as-cast alloy has two segregated BCC phases in W-Ta-rich dendritic and Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions.
The proposed tests above 700 °C do not reconstruct the reported room-temperature-to-500 °C quasi-static compression, indentation, and room-temperature scratch measurements.
The prediction of lower HEA yield strength contradicts the observed substantially higher strength relative to tungsten across the tested temperature range.
The cited evidence concerns transformation mechanisms in nickel superalloys and FCC/HCP CrMnFeCoNi alloys and does not establish a comparable transformation in this BCC refractory alloy.
explanation: The response addresses the general comparison of ductility and toughness against pure tungsten and offers a genuinely falsifiable in situ experiment. However, its central mechanism, material state, temperature regime, and strength prediction conflict with the target. It omits the observed dual-BCC solidification segregation, the measured 25–200 °C crack-disappearance behavior, the 500 °C strength advantage, and the scratch-toughness comparison. The proposed transformation mechanism is an unsupported extrapolation from crystallographically and chemically different alloy systems. Thus it is novel and experimentally discriminable, but neither a reconstruction nor a sufficiently evidence-grounded alternative for WTaTiVZr.
